Literature suggests that feature selection mechanisms like Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE) or Weight Predictor Networks can mitigate overfitting in small-sample, high-dimensional settings. To address the train/test gap and reduce noise from irrelevant features, we propose three distinct strategies: 1) A single Random Forest with aggressive pruning to prevent overfitting; 2) An ensemble using RFE for feature selection before training a Gradient Boosting model (leveraging evidence on RFE); 3) A pipeline combining PCA dimensionality reduction with a Logistic Regression classifier (testing linear separability after dimensionality reduction).
